findings.claim: mode() returns the maximum value (last element after sorting) instead of the statistical mode (most frequently occurring value). For example, mode([1, 2, 2, 9]) returns 9 instead of 2, and the existing tests do not exercise mode() at all (only mean and median are tested per test/stats.test.js and the test report).
findings.requiredAction: Implement mode() to count value frequencies and return the most frequent value (define behavior for ties), and add tests covering mode().

findings.claim: mode() mutates its input array via in-place values.sort(), unlike median() which sorts a copy ([...values].sort). Callers passing an array to mode() will have their array reordered as a side effect.
findings.requiredAction: Sort a copy of the input (e.g., const sorted = [...values].sort(...)) or compute frequencies without mutating the caller's array.
